Order:

(Per the Hon'ble Dr. Justice Shameem Akther) Mr. Mohd. Jahangeer, the petitioner, has filed this Habeas Corpus petition on behalf of his son, Shaik Azaharuddin @ Azhar, aged about 21 years, the detenu, challenging the detention order vide No.10/PD-CELL/CYB/2021, dated 04.02.2021, passed by the respondent No.2, Commissioner of Police, Cyberabad Commissionerate, wherein, the detenu was detained under Section 3(2) of the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers,
Dacoits, Drug-Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders, Land-Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders, Cyber Crime Offenders & White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short, "P.D. Act"), and the consequential confirmation order vide G.O.Rt.No.900, General Administration (Spl. (Law & Order)) Department, dated 12.04.2021,
passed by respondent No.1.
2.

Heard the submissions of Mr. Khaja Ziauddin, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri A.Manoj Kumar, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home representing the learned Additional Advocate General for the respondents and perused the record.
Dr.SA, J & NTR, J 3.

The background facts of the case, in brief, are that by relying two criminal cases registered against the detenu, viz., Crime Nos.910/2019 and 832/2020 of Mailardevpally Police Station, the respondent No.2-Commissioner of Police, Cyberabad Commissionerate, passed the impugned detention order, dated 04.02.2021.
According to the respondent No.2, the detenu is a 'Goonda'.

He engaged himself in acts of goondaism by committing gruesome and brutal murder of two persons in an organized manner, in the limits of Cyberabad Police Commissionerate, and thus created panic,
terror and fear in the minds of general public, thereby disturbing the public order and peace and tranquility in the area.
The unlawful activities of the detenu have been causing a feeling of insecurity in the minds of public on a regular basis, which is prejudicial to maintenance of public order.

Hence, this Writ Petition before this Court.

4. The learned counsel for the petitioner vehemently contended that the impugned detention order is vague, irrelevant, improper, against the principles of natural justice and has been passed in a mechanical manner and without application of mind.
The detenu is falsely implicated in the cases relied by the detaining authority.
The alleged criminal activities of the detenu, in any event, would not satisfy the word 'goonda'.
The detaining authority has not applied its mind to the facts and circumstances of the case, while passing the Dr.SA, J & NTR, J impugned detention order.
The detenu was granted conditional bail in Crime No.910/2019 and mandatory/statutory bail in Crime No.832/2020 by the Courts concerned.
Hence, there was no need to invoke the draconian preventive detention laws against the detenu, since he would be well within the surveillance of police.
The conditions imposed in the bail orders were sufficient to prevent the detenu from fleeing from justice.
It would be unjust if every person involved in a crime is incarcerated by invoking the draconian Preventive Detention laws, even before proving his guilt or otherwise by putting him at trial.

When the Courts thought it fit to release the detenu and released him on bail in the cases relied by the detaining authority, sending him again to prison on surmises, conjectures and apprehensions by invoking preventive detention laws is unjustified.
In order to pass a detention order, there has to be some proximity in time to provide a rational nexus between the incidents relied by the detaining authority and the satisfaction arrived by it.
In the instant case, there is no nexus between the offences alleged to be committed by the detenu warranting the respondent No.2 to pass the impugned detention order.
The material papers supplied to the detenu are not in the language known to him and some papers are illegible.

Further, the sponsoring authority has not placed the orders of bail granted to the detenu before the detaining authority and as such, the subjective satisfaction recorded by the detaining authority for preventively detaining the detenu is tainted and illegal.

Invoking preventive detention laws against a person is very harsh and unconstitutional,
unless there is a brazen conduct, which affects the even tempo of public life.
The said brazen conduct is missing in the present case.
Thus, the impugned order of preventive detention is ex facie illegal.
Dr.SA, J & NTR, J
Moreover, the cases alleged against the detenu do not add up to "disturbing the public order".
They are confined within the ambit and scope of the word "law and order".
Since the offences alleged are under Indian Penal Code, the detenu can certainly be tried under the Penal Code.
Thus, there was no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention laws.
Hence, the impugned detention order tantamounts to colourable exercise of power.
Preventive detention cannot be made a substitute to punitive detention.

The detaining authority has to be extremely careful while passing the detention order, since the detention ipso facto adversely affects the fundamental right of personal liberty enjoyed by the people under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
Thus, the detention order and the consequential confirmation order are legally unsustainable and ultimately, prayed to set aside the same and allow the writ petition as prayed for.
In support of his contentions, the learned counsel for the petitioner relied on a decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Champion R. Sangma Vs. State of Meghalaya and another1.

On the other hand, Sri A.Manoj Kumar, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home,
appearing for the respondents, supported the impugned detention order and submitted the detenu engaged himself in unlawful activities by committing gruesome and brutal murder of two persons in public places, in an organized way, in the limits of Cyberabad Police Commissionerate.

The unlawful activities of the detenu were creating large scale fear, terror and panic among the people and thereby, adversely affecting the public (2015) 16 Supreme Court Cases 253 Dr.SA, J & NTR, J order.

In the first crime, i.e., Crime No.910/2018, the detenu picked up a quarrel with the deceased due to previous enmity and stabbed the deceased with a knife and caused heavy bleeding injuries which resulted in death of the deceased.

In the second crime, i.e., Crime No.832/2020, the detenu and his associates picked up quarrel with the deceased and stabbed him with knives and caused multiple bleeding injuries resulting in his death and escaped on their bikes by wielding the knives on the streets with an intention to create panic in the minds of local public.

The detenu was also earlier involved two crimes of robbery and theft, i.e., Crime Nos.174/2018 of Charminar police station and 472/2019 of Mylardevpally police station under the limits of Cyberabad and Hyderabad Police Commissionerates.

Further, after release on bail in the subject two crimes relied by the detaining authority, the detenu again involved in a case of attempt to murder vide Crime No.8/2021 of Chatrinaka police station on 08.01.2021.
With a view to prevent the detenu from further indulging in such dangerous activities in the interest of the society, the impugned detention order was passed.
The subjective satisfaction reached by the detaining authority for preventively detaining the detenu is not tainted or illegal.

The detenu was served with the detention order, grounds for detention and corresponding documents and translation copies in the language known to him on 05.02.2021 and the detenu acknowledged the same.

Further, the Advisory Board, in its review meeting held on 15.03.2021, upon hearing the detenu and the concerned investigating officials and upon considering the entire material placed before it, rendered its opinion that there is sufficient cause for detention of the detenu.

On considering the opinion of the Advisory Board and upon considering Dr.SA, J &
NTR, J the entire material independently, the Government confirmed the impugned detention order, vide G.O.Rt.No.900, dated 12.04.2021.
Therefore, the detaining authority was legally justified in passing the impugned detention order.

All the mandatory provisions and the safeguards envisaged under the law were strictly followed while passing the impugned detention order and hence, the impugned detention order does not suffer from illegality or impropriety and ultimately,
prayed to dismiss the Writ Petition.

6. In view of the submissions made by both sides, the point that arises for determination in this Writ Petition is:
"Whether the impugned detention order, dated 04.02.2021, passed by respondent No.2 and the consequential confirmation order, dated 12.04.2021, passed by respondent No.1 are liable to be set aside?"
7. POINT:

As per the record, by relying on two criminal cases registered against the detenu, viz.,
Cr.No.910/2019 and 832/2020 of Mylardevpalli Police Station, the respondent No.2-Commissioner of Police, Cyberabad Commissionerate, passed the impugned detention order, dated 04.02.2021.
According to the respondent No.2, the detenu is a 'goonda'.

In order to prevent Dr.SA, J & NTR, J the detenu from further indulging in such highly dangerous and illegal activities, which are detrimental to the public order, the impugned detention order, dated 04.02.2021, was passed, which was confirmed by the Government by order, dated 12.04.2021.

Shaik Jagangir, is alleged to be a 'goonda', as he has been habitually indulging in the acts of goondaism on a regular basis and has been causing a feeling of insecurity in the minds of general public in the limits of Cyberabad Police Commissionerate and his illegal activities have been adversely affecting the maintenance of public order and peace in the area.

Earlier when the detenu asked the deceased for Rs.10,000/- to meet his personal needs, the deceased denied.

Since then, the detenu bore grudge against the Dr.SA, J & NTR, J deceased and decided to eliminate him and shared the same with Hannan, who agreed to give his knife to the detenu for commission of offence and both of them waited for an opportunity to eliminate the deceased.

On 18.12.2019 at about 20:00 hours, when the detenu and Hannan were consuming liquor on the roof top of an under- construction house near the residence of the deceased, the deceased and his friend came there.

The deceased ran into his house making hue and cry and the detenu chased the deceased and entered his house with an intention to stab him again, but due to hues and cries of the family members of the deceased, the detenu fled away with the knife.
Immediately the deceased was taken to Osmania General Hospital and the duty doctor declared that the deceased was brought dead.
10. In the second crime, i.e., Crime No.832/2020, it is alleged that the detenu, Syed Kamran Hashmi, Md.Hannan and Md.Khan are friends.
One day Syed Kamran Hashmi informed the deceased and other friends that the deceased, who resides in adjacent street, used to ask him the reason for roaming in their streets unnecessarily.
Syed Kamran Hashmi felt ashamed with the questions of the deceased and decided to eliminate him and sought the help of the detenu in doing so.
The detenu accepted the proposal of Syed Kamran Hashmi and waited for the right time to eliminate the Dr.SA, J & NTR, J deceased.
On 05.09.2020 midnight at about 00:30 hrs, while the detenu along with his aforesaid associates were proceeding on two bikes through Owaisi Hills, they found the deceased there.
Syed Kamran Hashmi informed the detenu that it was the right to eliminate the deceased.

Thereupon, the detenu deliberately picked up quarrel with the deceased saying as to why he did not greet the detenu for which, the deceased replied that he does not know the detenu and that he was not an 'awara' like the detenu and his associates.
On that, the detenu and his associates got down from the bikes and stabbed the deceased with knives.

The deceased received severe blunt injuries in his left armpit, stomach, side ribs, chin and cheek and he fell down on the ground and later the detenu and his associates fled away on their bikes by wielding the knives in the streets with an intention to create panic in the minds of local public.
11. In the first crime, i.e., Crime No.910/2019, the detenu was arrested on 21.12.2019.

The detenu moved bail application before the Court concerned on 04.03.2020 and the Court concerned granted bail to the detenu, vide order, 16.03.2020, passed in Crl.M.P.No.1040 of 2020 and the detenu was released from jail on 19.03.2020.
In the second crime, i.e., Crime No.832 of 2020, the detenu was arrested on 08.09.2020.
However, the detenu was granted mandatory/statutory bail under Section 167(2) of Cr.P.C. by the Court on concerned on 07.12.2020 and he was released from jail on 14.12.2020.

Thus, it is evident that the detenu, after release on conditional bail in the first crime, i.e.,
Crime No.910/2019, again committed the second crime on 05.09.2020.
It establishes that the conditions imposed in the bail order of the first crime did not deter him from committing second Dr.SA, J & NTR, J grave offence of murder.
Two persons were killed without there being any fault or reason.
Neither they gave any provocation nor created any circumstance that lead to commission of murders.
They have no animosity, grudge or were causing any obstacles or disturbance in the life of the detenu and his associates.
They are innocent persons.
They had not directly or indirectly created any circumstance against the detenu and his associates to cause the subject deaths.

The modus operandi and the circumstances that lead to commission of two incidents certainly affects public order and not merely law and order, inasmuch as the reach, effect and potentiality of the acts purport to disturb the even tempo of the life of the community i.e. the people of that locality.

The acts of the detenu cannot be termed as only law and order problem but it is public order problem, as assessed by the detaining authority, who is supposed to safeguard and protect the interest of public.

The demeanor of the detenu in the incidents taken into account by the detaining authority would Mohd Jahangeer vs The State Of Telangana on 29 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101494658/
5 certainly terrorize the people, creates panic, danger alarm and a feeling of insecurity among them,
which is prejudicial to maintenance of public order.
12. It is apt to state the legal parameters for testing the validity of preventive detention fundamentally vary from that of punitive detention.

entities.text: Mohd Jahangeer vs The State Of Telangana
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The power of preventive detention is a precautionary power exercised in reasonable anticipation.
It may or may not relate to an offence.
It is not a parallel proceeding.
It does not overlap with prosecution, even if it relies on certain facts for which prosecution may be launched or may have been launched.
An order of preventive detention may be made before or during prosecution, Dr.SA, J & NTR, J with or without prosecution, in anticipation or after discharge or even acquittal.
Pendency of prosecution is no bar to an order of preventive detention.
An order of preventive detention is also not a bar to prosecution.
13. In the case of Madhu Limaye Vs. Sub-Divisional Magistrate2.

The Hon'ble Apex Court held as follows:
"The acts which disturb public tranquility or are breaches of the peace should not be given a narrow meaning, but should be given a liberal interpretation.
For the expression 'in the interest of public order' is very wide amplitude."

14. In the case of Commissioner of Police & Others Vs. C.Anita (Smt.)3, the Hon'ble Apex Court examined the issue of "public order"
and "law and order" and observed as follows:
"The crucial issue is whether the activities of the detenu were prejudicial to public order.

entities.text: Commissioner of Police & Others Vs. C.Anita (Smt.)3,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: While the expression "law and order" is wider in scope inasmuch as contravention of law always affects order, "public order" has a narrower ambit, and public order could be affected by only such contravention which affects the community or the public at large.
Public order is the even tempo of life of the community taking the country as a whole or even a specified locality.
The distinction between the areas of "law and order" and "public order" is one of the degree and extent of the reach of the act in question on society.
It is the potentiality of the act to disturb the even tempo of life of the community which makes it prejudicial to the maintenance of the public order.
If a contravention in its effect is confined only to a few individuals directly involved as distinct from a wide spectrum of the public, it could raise problem of law and order only.

It is the length, magnitude and intensity of the terror wave unleashed by a particular eruption of disorder that helps to distinguish it as an act affecting "public order" from that concerning "law and order".

The question to ask is: "Does it lead to disturbance of the current life of the community so as to amount to a disturbance of the public order or does it affect merely an individual leaving the tranquility of the society undisturbed?"

This question has to be faced in every case on its facts."
15.
In Arun Ghosh Vs. State of Bengal4, the Hon'ble Apex court held as follows:

sentences.text: "An act by itself is not determinant of its own gravity.
In its quality it may not differ from another but in its potentiality it may (1970) 3 SCC 746 (2004) 7 SCC 467 AIR 1970 SC 1228 Dr.SA, J & NTR, J be very different.
Take the case of assault on girls.
A guest at a hotel may kiss or make advances to half a dozen chamber maids.
He may annoy them and also the management but he does not cause disturbance of public order.
He may even have a fracas with the friends of one of the girls but even then it would be a case of breach of law and order only.
Take another case of a man who molests women in lonely places.
As a result of his activities girls going to colleges and schools are in constant danger and fear.
Women going for their ordinary business are afraid of being waylaid and assaulted.
The activity of this man in its essential quality is not different from the act of the other man but in its potentiality and in its affect upon the public tranquillity there is a vast difference.
The act of the man who molests the girls in lonely places causes a disturbance in the even tempo of living which is the first requirement of public order.
He disturbs the society and the community.

His act makes all the women apprehensive of their honour and he can be said to be causing disturbance of public order and not merely committing individual actions which may be taken note of by the criminal prosecution agencies.

16. A person who has been habitually engaging himself in unlawful acts of committing brutal and gruesome murders, which create a sense of insecurity in the minds of public, pose a great threat to maintenance of peace and public tranquility in the society and such activities are obviously prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.

In the instant case, the incidents taken into account by the detaining authority have been causing serious disturbance of peace and tranquillity in the locality and inevitably attracted attention of the residents nearby and the people of the locality naturally got quite panic-stricken and feel frightened to move freely to perform their normal daily activities.

Thus, we reject the contention raised by learned counsel for the petitioner that the cases relied by the detaining authority does not add up to 'disturbance of public order', but they are confined within the ambit and scope of the word 'law and order'.
17.
In Champion R Sangma's case supra relied by the learned counsel for the petitioner, the detention order was passed while the detenu therein was already in custody.
It is not so in the instant Dr.SA, J & NTR, J case.
Hence, the said decision is distinguishable on facts from the case on hand.

18. As per the clause (g) of Section 2 of the P.D.Act, a "goonda" means a person, who either by himself or as a member of or leader of a gang, habitually commits, or attempts to commit or abets the commission of offences punishable under Chapter XVI or Chapter XVII or Chapter XXII of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.label: PROVISION

sentences.text: 19. The personal liberty of an individual, which the law preserves and protects, can also be taken away by following the procedure established by law, when it is used to jeopardize the public good.

In the instant case, the commission of alleged offences, as indicated in the above table, clearly demonstrates that the detenu, despite of his arrest in Crime No.910/2019 and release on conditional bail, did not mend his attitude and again indulged in another gruesome offence of murder, within six months after coming out from jail.

It is also evident from the record that after release of the Mohd Jahangeer vs The State Of Telangana on 29 December, 2021 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101494658/
7 detenu on mandatory/statutory bail in second crime, i.e., Crime No.832/2020, he again indulged in a subsequent offence of attempt to murder, vide Crime No.08/2021, dated 08.01.2021 of Chatrinaka Police Station.

sentences.text:
So it is imperative upon the officers concerned to pass the impugned detention order,
since the acts of the detenu created terror and panic in the locality, which is prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.

The detaining authority, having satisfied that the cases registered against the detenu under the Penal Code had no deterrent effect and the detenu was not amenable to the ordinary law of land, passed the impugned detention order.

Here, it is apt to refer to the decision of Dr.SA, J & NTR, J the Hon'ble Apex Court in Subrahmanian Vs. State of Tamil Nadu5,
wherein, it was held as follows:
It is well settled that the court does not interfere with the subjective satisfaction reached by the detaining authority except in exceptional and extremely limited grounds.

entities.text: Subrahmanian Vs. State of Tamil Nadu5
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The court cannot substitute its own opinion for that of the detaining authority when the grounds of detention are precise, pertinent, proximate and relevant, that sufficiency of grounds is not for the court but for the detaining authority for the formation of subjective satisfaction that the detention of a person with a view to preventing him from acting in any manner prejudicial to public order is required and that such satisfaction is subjective and not objective.

The object of the law of preventive detention is not punitive but only preventive and further that the action of the executive in detaining a person being only precautionary, normally, the matter has necessarily to be left to the discretion of the executive authority.
It is not practicable to lay down objective rules of conduct in an exhaustive manner.
The satisfaction of the detaining authority, therefore, is considered to be of primary importance with certain latitude in the exercise of its discretion.

20. In the instant case, the detaining authority had sufficient material to record subjective satisfaction that the detention of the detenu was necessary to maintain public order and even tempo of life of the community.
The order of detention does not suffer from any illegality.
The grounds of detention, as indicated in the impugned order, are found to be pertinent, proximate, relevant and in tune with the provisions of the P.D.Act.

The incidents highlighted in the grounds of detention coupled with the definite indication as to the impact thereof, which have been precisely stated in the grounds of detention, clearly substantiate the subjective satisfaction arrived at by the detaining authority.

Since the detenu was granted bail in the two crimes relied by the detaining authority and moving freely in the public, there is nothing wrong on the part of the detaining authority in raising an apprehension that there is every possibility of the detenu committing similar offences in view of his criminal intent to strike terror in the public at large, which would again certainly affect 2012 (4)
SCC 699 Dr.SA, J & NTR, J the public order.
The grounds of detention, as indicated in the impugned order, are found to be relevant and in tune with the provisions of the Telangana Preventive Detention Act.

The material placed on record further reveals that the order of detention, along with the grounds of detention and the material referred to and relied upon in the grounds of detention,
were supplied to the detenue in the language known to him, i.e., Urdu, besides English.
The subjective satisfaction reached by the detaining authority is not tainted or illegal, on any account.
The acts of the detenu cannot be effectively dealt with under the provisions of Indian Penal Code.

We do not see any merit in this Writ Petition and as such, it is liable to be dismissed.
22. The Writ Petition is, accordingly, dismissed.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, in this Writ Petition, shall stand closed.

Further, the sponsoring authority has not placed the orders of bail granted to the detenu before the detaining authority and as such, the subjective satisfaction recorded by the detaining authority for preventively detaining the detenu is tainted and illegal.
Invoking preventive detention laws against a person is very harsh and unconstitutional,
unless there is a brazen conduct, which affects the even tempo of public life.
Thus, the impugned order of preventive detention is ex facie illegal.
They are confined within the ambit and scope of the word "law and order".
Since the offences alleged are under Indian Penal Code, the detenu can certainly be tried under the Penal Code.
Thus, there was no need for the detaining authority to invoke the draconian preventive detention laws.
Hence, the impugned detention order tantamounts to colourable exercise of power.
Preventive detention cannot be made a substitute to punitive detention.
The detaining authority has to be extremely careful while passing the detention order, since the detention ipso facto adversely affects the fundamental right of personal liberty enjoyed by the people under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.
On the other hand, Sri A.Manoj Kumar, learned Assistant Government Pleader for Home,
appearing for the respondents, supported the impugned detention order and submitted the detenu engaged himself in unlawful activities by committing gruesome and brutal murder of two persons in public places, in an organized way, in the limits of Cyberabad Police Commissionerate.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
They had not directly or indirectly created any circumstance against the detenu and his associates to cause the subject deaths.
The modus operandi and the circumstances that lead to commission of two incidents certainly affects public order and not merely law and order, inasmuch as the reach, effect and potentiality of the acts purport to disturb the even tempo of the life of the community i.e. the people of that locality.
The acts of the detenu cannot be termed as only law and order problem but it is public order problem, as assessed by the detaining authority, who is supposed to safeguard and protect the interest of public.
The power of preventive detention is a precautionary power exercised in reasonable anticipation.
In the instant case, the incidents taken into account by the detaining authority have been causing serious disturbance of peace and tranquillity in the locality and inevitably attracted attention of the residents nearby and the people of the locality naturally got quite panic-stricken and feel frightened to move freely to perform their normal daily activities.
In the instant case, the commission of alleged offences, as indicated in the above table, clearly demonstrates that the detenu, despite of his arrest in Crime No.910/2019 and release on conditional bail, did not mend his attitude and again indulged in another gruesome offence of murder, within six months after coming out from jail.
So it is imperative upon the officers concerned to pass the impugned detention order,
since the acts of the detenu created terror and panic in the locality, which is prejudicial to the maintenance of public order.
The order of detention does not suffer from any illegality.
Since the detenu was granted bail in the two crimes relied by the detaining authority and moving freely in the public, there is nothing wrong on the part of the detaining authority in raising an apprehension that there is every possibility of the detenu committing similar offences in view of his criminal intent to strike terror in the public at large, which would again certainly affect 2012 (4)
SCC 699 Dr.SA, J & NTR, J the public order.
The grounds of detention, as indicated in the impugned order, are found to be relevant and in tune with the provisions of the Telangana Preventive Detention Act.
The material placed on record further reveals that the order of detention, along with the grounds of detention and the material referred to and relied upon in the grounds of detention,
were supplied to the detenue in the language known to him, i.e., Urdu, besides English.
The subjective satisfaction reached by the detaining authority is not tainted or illegal, on any account.
The acts of the detenu cannot be effectively dealt with under the provisions of Indian Penal Code.
